summary: Describes an architecture from Cisco for lawfully authorized interception and monitoring of communications in IP networks. Service providers face legal and regulatory demands that vary by country, and the document sets out a common approach to meet them. It is informational and was not an IETF standard.

eli5.summary: When a court legally orders it, a phone company may need to listen in on a particular line. This memo describes one company's design for doing that in computer networks.

questions: how does lawful intercept work in ip networks
subtitle: A design for intercepting and monitoring communications in IP networks.

tldr.problem: Service providers worldwide face legal and regulatory requirements to intercept communications (voice and data) in IP networks. Although requirements vary by country, many share common needs despite different delivery formats.
tldr.mechanism: The architecture defines a reference model with components (Intercept Access Points, Mediation Device, administration function) and standard interfaces that separate the provisioning and interception from the delivery to law enforcement, allowing operators to adapt to country-specific requirements.
tldr.outcome: A vendor-specific design that provides a practical solution for meeting diverse legal requirements while keeping the interception undetectable to the target and protecting against unauthorized access.

today: RFC 3924 is an Informational RFC and describes Cisco's approach to lawful intercept architecture. It is not an Internet standard but has been influential in shaping how service providers implement interception compliance.

sections.title: Introduction and Requirements
sections.content:
Lawful intercept is the legally authorized interception and monitoring of communications of a target subject. Service providers are asked to meet legal and regulatory requirements for intercepting both voice and data communications in IP networks across many countries. Although these requirements vary from country to country, some common themes emerge.

The key requirements that drive the architecture include: the intercept must be undetectable to the target, mechanisms must prevent unauthorized personnel from performing intercepts, separate delivery of intercept-related information (IRI) from actual content, means to correlate the two, provisions for decryption if the service provider holds keys, support for multiple simultaneous intercepts on one subject, and strict controls to prevent unauthorized information delivery to law enforcement.
sections.eli5: A court can order a phone company to listen to someone's calls. The company needs a design that: hides the listening, stops bad actors from listening, keeps info organized, and prevents mistakes.

sections.title: Reference Model and Components
sections.content:
The architecture defines a generic reference model with distinct components. The Lawful Intercept Administration Function is the entry point where law enforcement delivers court orders and authorized personnel provision the intercept. The Intercept Access Point (IAP) is a network device (often an edge router or switch) that performs the actual interception. Two types of IAPs exist: a Content IAP that intercepts the actual IP traffic of interest, and an IRI IAP that collects intercept-related information such as called and calling numbers. The Mediation Device (MD) is the central hub that receives interception requests, collects data from IAPs, packages it in country-specific formats, and delivers it to the Law Enforcement Agency (LEA). The MD can replicate data for multiple simultaneous intercepts.

The placement of content intercepts is critical: they occur on devices in the normal packet path (such as an edge router) within the service provider's network, not by re-routing, to remain undetectable to the target.
sections.eli5: The design has a few parts: an admin person enters the court order, network routers grab the traffic and call info, a mediation device packages it right, and sends it to police. No one can secretly turn it on.

sections.title: Interfaces Between Components
sections.content:
The reference model defines multiple interfaces (labeled a through h) between components. The HI1 interface (a) is where law enforcement provides intercept information to the administration function. The MD Provisioning interface (b) carries parameters such as target identifier, intercept duration, and intercept type to the mediation device. The IRI IAP Provisioning interface (c) specifies which target and for how long the IRI IAP should collect data. The Content Intercept Provisioning interface (d) commands the content IAP to begin interception, using SNMPv3 protocol and specifying filter criteria, the mediation device destination address, and encapsulation parameters.

The IRI to MD interface (e) is internal, delivering collected intercept-related information to the mediation device. The Content to MD interface (f) carries the actual intercepted IP packets. The HI2 interface (g) delivers formatted IRI to law enforcement, and the HI3 interface (h) delivers formatted content to law enforcement. Interfaces (g) and (h) may vary from country to country.
sections.eli5: Different parts of the system talk to each other through defined channels: police tell the admin function what to do, the admin tells the mediation device, the mediation device tells the routers where to send captured stuff, routers send the data back, and mediation device sends everything to police in the right format.

sections.title: Voice over IP and Data Interception
sections.content:
The same reference model applies to both voice over IP services and data services, though with different details. For voice over IP, a call control entity (such as a SIP proxy or H.323 gatekeeper) that owns the target subscriber is provisioned with intercept parameters. This CCE generates IRI containing media signaling information such as endpoint IP addresses and port numbers from the SDP or H.245 protocol. Armed with this address information, the mediation device can locate the appropriate content IAP (likely an edge router or PSTN gateway) and command it to intercept the voice stream based on IP addresses and UDP ports.

For data services, the IRI IAP might be a RADIUS server that handles registration and authentication. The IRI collected includes registration or de-registration times and addressing information. Once the mediation device has suitable address information for the content tap, it requests that the content IAP (typically an edge router) begin interception. The same SNMPv3-based protocol and encapsulation format work for both voice and data, making the architecture independent of application type.
sections.eli5: For phone calls, the system grabs the routing info (who calls whom and where packets go), then tells a router to listen. For data, it finds when someone logs in and their address, then tells a router to capture their traffic. Both use the same basic machinery.

sections.title: Security and Access Control
sections.content:
Given the sensitive nature of lawful intercept, stringent security measures are necessary. All interfaces must support strong cryptographic authentication to establish principal identity and correlate identity with action. Interfaces should provide cryptographic message integrity checking such as HMAC-MD5 to counter replay attacks, and may require encryption for privacy. Both the content and IRI IAPs must protect the identity of the intercept subject and the very existence of an intercept.

For the content request interface (d), SNMPv3 security mechanisms are used natively. The IAP should support protection of the TAP MIB from disclosure or unauthorized control by restricting access to SNMPv3 USM users who have established keys and possess proper VACM (View-based Access Control Model) views. Additionally, the TAP MIB should be segregated so only operators of sufficient privilege level can create VACM views that include it, preventing lower-privilege staff from discovering intercepts or creating unauthorized ones.
sections.eli5: All messages between parts need cryptographic protection so only the right people can see and change them. The mediation device and routers must be locked down so only special admins can turn interception on.
